planting.note: Plant dormant crowns or plugs in October in zone 9 for a winter-into-spring crop; Winterstar (FL 05-107) is a University of Florida IFAS release from the Gulf Coast Research and Education Center bred to complement the industry-standard Festival and Florida Radiance releases in Gulf-latitude short-day plasticulture.

directions: Plant dormant crowns or plug transplants with the crown at soil level in raised, plastic-mulched beds in full sun; Winterstar was released in 2011 from a 2005 cross of 'Florida Radiance' and 'Earlibrite' by the UF/IFAS Gulf Coast Research and Education Center in Balm, Florida, and was positioned to complement rather than replace the two industry-standard cultivars of the era, Festival and Florida Radiance. As with other short-day cultivars grown in the Deep South annual plasticulture system, set out fresh crowns each fall on raised, drip-irrigated, plastic-mulched beds and treat the planting strictly as a winter annual, since plants decline rapidly once summer heat arrives. Fruit ripens on a schedule comparable to Radiance, with good early-season production valuable for growers and home gardeners who want fruit on the table before the main winter flush.

common_name: Florida Pearl Strawberry (UF/IFAS White-Fruited Pineberry Release)

planting.note: Plant dormant crowns or plugs in October in zone 9 for a winter-into-spring crop; Florida Pearl ('FL 16.78-109') was released in 2020 by the UF/IFAS strawberry breeding program as the first named white-fruited pineberry cultivar bred specifically for Gulf-latitude short-day annual production.

directions: Plant dormant crowns or plug transplants with the crown at soil level in raised, plastic-mulched beds in full sun; Florida Pearl is the University of Florida IFAS strawberry breeding program's first white-fruited 'pineberry' release, developed by crossing descendants of Japanese white strawberries with red Florida short-day breeding lines for yield, disease resistance, and adaptation to Gulf-latitude winter production. Fruit is pure white internally with a white-to-pink-blushed exterior, red achenes, moderate gloss, and a distinctive low-acid flavor with aromatic notes of pineapple or apricot; the plant is denser and shorter-stemmed than Florida Brilliance. Because pineberries are low in self-fertility, interplant with a standard red-fruiting short-day cultivar such as Florida Brilliance or Sweet Charlie to ensure adequate pollination and fruit set; expect yields roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of a standard red cultivar. Treat strictly as a winter annual, planting fresh crowns each fall on raised, drip-irrigated, plastic-mulched beds.

common_name: Florida Ember Strawberry (UF/IFAS Neopestalotiopsis-Resistant Organic-Adapted Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant dormant crowns or plugs October 1–15 in zone 9 for a winter-into-spring crop; Florida Ember ('FL 20.80-4') is a 2024 UF/IFAS release bred at the Gulf Coast Research and Education Center for open-field and organic short-day plasticulture production in Gulf-latitude climates.

directions: Plant dormant crowns or plug transplants with the crown at soil level in raised, plastic-mulched beds in full sun, ideally set out October 1–15; Florida Ember is a 2024 release from the University of Florida IFAS Gulf Coast Research and Education Center bred as an early, disease-resistant companion to Florida Brilliance. It carries the strongest disease resistance package of the current UF short-day lineup, including the lowest susceptibility to Neopestalotiopsis fruit and leaf spot of any UF cultivar, along with moderate resistance to anthracnose, charcoal rot, crown rot, and botrytis — traits that make it especially well suited to humid Gulf South conditions and to organic production, where it performs best in open fields rather than high tunnels. The robust, compact plants carry medium-to-large, uniform conic berries with bright red skin and a light red to nearly white interior, low acid, and high Brix sweetness comparable to Florida Medallion, along with unusually good rain resistance for a short-day cultivar. Treat as a winter annual, replacing crowns each fall.

common_name: Florida Encore Strawberry (UF/IFAS High-Yield Firm-Fleshed Shipping Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant dormant crowns or plugs October 12–22 in zone 9 for a winter-into-spring crop; Florida Encore ('FL 20.34-183') is a 2024 UF/IFAS release bred at the Gulf Coast Research and Education Center as a firmer-fleshed, higher-yield improvement on Florida Brilliance for Gulf-latitude short-day production.

directions: Plant dormant crowns or plug transplants with the crown at soil level in raised, plastic-mulched beds in full sun, ideally set out October 12–22; Florida Encore is a 2024 release from the University of Florida IFAS Gulf Coast Research and Education Center bred as an improvement on Florida Brilliance. The vigorous plants produce a heavy first inflorescence that drives high early yields from mid-October plantings and continues into steady winter and spring harvests. Fruit is large, glossy, and evenly red both outside and in, with moderate acid and Brix and notably firm flesh that gives Encore excellent shelf life and shipping quality compared to most short-day Florida cultivars. It is moderately resistant to anthracnose fruit rot and phytophthora crown rot but moderately susceptible to Colletotrichum crown rot and charcoal rot, so maintain good bed drainage and avoid planting into fields with a history of soilborne disease. Treat as a winter annual, replacing crowns each fall.

common_name: Florida Medallion Strawberry (UF/IFAS Sweet Aromatic Winter Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant dormant crowns or plugs in October in zone 9 for a winter-into-spring crop; Florida Medallion is a 2020 UF/IFAS release from the Gulf Coast Research and Education Center that Florida growers have steadily expanded plantings of since its introduction alongside Florida Brilliance and Sensation.

directions: Plant dormant crowns or plug transplants with the crown at soil level in raised, plastic-mulched beds in full sun; Florida Medallion was released in 2020 by the University of Florida IFAS Gulf Coast Research and Education Center and has become a steadily more widely planted alternative to Florida Brilliance and Sensation in commercial Gulf-latitude short-day production. The robust, medium-vigor plants carry medium-to-large, uniform conic fruit with bright red skin and a light red to nearly white interior; low acid and high Brix give it a sweet, intensely fruity, aromatic flavor that stands out among subtropical short-day cultivars, making it popular with growers selling direct to consumers as well as through wholesale channels. As with other short-day strawberries in the Deep South annual system, treat it strictly as a winter annual, setting out fresh crowns each fall on raised, drip-irrigated, plastic-mulched beds for harvest from winter into spring.

common_name: Benicia Strawberry (California-Bred Short-Day Cultivar for Gulf South Winter Production)

planting.note: Plant dormant crowns or plugs in October–November in zone 9 for a winter-into-spring crop; Benicia is a University of California short-day (June-bearing type) release, US Plant Patent PP22542, that placed among the top performers alongside Festival and Sweet Ann in LSU AgCenter strawberry variety trials for Louisiana growing conditions.

directions: Plant dormant crowns or plug transplants with the crown at soil level in raised, plastic-mulched beds in full sun; Benicia was developed by the University of California strawberry breeding program as a short-day type suited to fall planting for winter and spring fruiting in mild subtropical climates. Though bred in California, it was trialed and recommended by the LSU AgCenter as one of the top-performing varieties — alongside Festival and Sweet Ann — for Louisiana home garden and Gulf South production, where its fall-set winter annual habit fits the same short-day plasticulture system used throughout the region. Plants are slightly more compact than Ventana but produce individual-plant yields greater than Camarosa, with larger, higher-quality fruit than Ventana at a comparable fruit count per plant. As with other short-day strawberries grown as annuals in zone 9, replace crowns each fall on raised, drip-irrigated, plastic-mulched beds and harvest from winter through spring before summer heat ends production.
